payload.label: Evaluate a writing-voice classifier on labelled passages
payload.job: Check how well a small classifier judges a writer's voice: validate the labelled challenge passages, plan the questions, ask the classifier each one, and report its choices, probabilities, abstentions and accuracy by criterion, family and source
payload.description: Give data, a challenge of labelled passages (schema book-voice-decider-challenge-v1, v2 or v3), and an action. validate checks the challenge (unique ids, one split per family, typed blocks, criteria, labels) and counts the model questions; plan returns the exact request each passage would send (the passage and only its criterion-scoped or pinned reference context, never the general context, which can hold labels); evaluate asks the classifier (the endpoint and model in the person's list:settings row for this tool, settings_record, as the person's store gives it and tools/settings reads it) and answers the report: every choice with its full probabilities, a decision that is the choice only when its probability is over the criterion's diagnostic minimum (else uncertain), confusion matrices and abstentions by criterion, family and source kind, and errors kept as errors, never passes; a section heading is judged over every source-bound chunk of its section (one fail fails it, all pass passes it). A reply whose model or serving identity differs from the classifier's health is an error. replies plays recorded exchanges in place of the classifier (a stand-in: a request with no recording is refused). check-report checks a stored report against its challenge (identity, request policy, every captured request and raw response). Nothing is trained and nothing is written; the person's passages and labels are input only.

data.description: A challenge: schema book-voice-decider-challenge-v1, v2 or v3; items each { id, family, split, text, origin.kind or source_kind, gold or checks, block_kind (v3) }; a single question and options (v1) or criteria (v2, v3: each { id, question, primitive one-of | true-or-false, options, reference_context and applies_to in v3, deterministic?, diagnostic_min_probability?, section_chunk_request? })

data_name.description: What the report calls the data (default request:data)

data_blake3.description: The BLAKE3 of the data's file bytes, when the data was read from a file (default: of the request's data)

settings_record.description: The person's list:settings row for this tool, record:setting:train-and-evaluate-a-writing-voice-classifier~<scope_kind>~<scope_id>, as the person's store gives it ({ id, type, value }), read with tools/settings; its settings are { endpoint, model, attempts?, workers? }

replies.description: Recorded exchanges { request, status, response } to play in place of the classifier

health.description: With replies: the classifier's recorded health ({ serving, device })

prior_report.description: A report to resume: kept only when everything it was made from is unchanged

include_evidence.description: Keep every request and raw response in the answer

output_schema.description: validate: { mode, items, criteria, request_policy, model_questions }; plan: { plans }; check-report: { valid, complete, covered, identity_assurance }; evaluate: the report (schema book-voice-decider-evaluation-v2: summary, items, errors, complete, serving_identity_assurance)

payload.label: Find where test passages also appear in a classifier's training rows
payload.job: Find whether the passages a classifier is tested on also appear in the rows it was trained on: the same text, the same family or the same whole request
payload.description: Give training_rows and target_rows (each a row, or a row with state, whose state holds target_text and may hold reader_context and reference_text), and optionally training_source and target_source ({ source_id, blake3, path, schema }). The answer lists every target whose text appears in a training row's target, reader context or reference (exact, or after NFKC, case and whitespace folding, on word boundaries, for targets of at least 16 characters; shorter ones are named unassessed), every same-family pair and every identical whole state. Source identities come back as safe tokens only, never paths. No match is only absence of these overlaps, never proof of independence.

state.target_text: The kettle boiled in four minutes, so we timed the pot.

payload.label: Train a writing-voice adapter on labelled rows
payload.job: Train a small LoRA adapter that judges a writer's voice from labelled training rows bound to their source passages
payload.description: Runs on the person's computer that holds the decider model snapshot and its frame (common.py, the folder decider_common_dir names, from the person's settings row for this tool). Only split train rows are taken; gold never enters the prompt; a provenance manifest binds every row to its source passage and criterion through the maintained request plan before the model loads. Writes the adapter and a receipt (BLAKE3 of the DATA, every setting) into a new folder; sends no request.

data.description: JSONL of training rows (book-voice-adapter-training-row-v1 or v2)

out.description: a new folder for the adapter

payload.label: Score labelled or unlabeled passages, or one draft, with a writing-voice adapter
payload.job: Score passages with a trained writing-voice adapter and report every probability, with the exposure of the passages to the training rows, or score one draft paragraph by paragraph
payload.description: Runs on the person's computer that holds the decider model snapshot. Validates the challenge with the maintained validator before weights load, binds the adapter and its receipt by BLAKE3, keeps every row's probabilities and the audit of what the adapter was trained on, and never invents accuracy for unlabeled rows. Draft mode (mode "draft") scores one draft text instead: its settings come from the person's own settings row (settings_record, the row record:setting:train-and-evaluate-a-writing-voice-classifier~person~<them> as selected from their database; its settings.draft gives adapter, base_model, criterion, min_paragraph_chars and bar) or the request itself, and it loads the Workshop's own decider frame. It splits the text at blank lines, keeps paragraphs whose words (web addresses left out) are shorter than min_paragraph_chars as skipped, scores every other one with the same request a v3 row gets, and answers paragraph_scores and body_min (the lowest p_pass) with no decision, and hands on the person's bar when their settings give one; the caller's check compares body_min with it.

mode.description: draft: score the one text given, paragraph by paragraph, in place of a challenge file

text.description: draft mode: the words of the draft; paragraphs are split at blank lines

base_model.description: draft mode: the decider model snapshot folder the adapter was trained on

criterion.description: draft mode: one v3 model criterion (id, question, options with one named pass, reference_context)

min_paragraph_chars.description: draft mode: a paragraph whose words (web addresses left out) are shorter than this is answered as skipped and not scored

decider_common_dir.description: the folder holding common.py; draft mode uses the Workshop's own (tools/fine-tune-a-small-model-on-a-persons-rules/read-data) when none is named

settings_record.description: draft mode: the person's settings row as selected from their database (record:setting:train-and-evaluate-a-writing-voice-classifier~person~<them>); its settings.draft gives every draft key the request does not

bar.description: draft mode: the lowest p_pass the person's voice accepts; handed back as given, for the caller's check

invoke.say: Runs on the person's computer that holds the decider model snapshot. Validates the challenge with the maintained validator before weights load, binds the adapter and its receipt by BLAKE3, keeps every row's probabilities and the audit of what the adapter was trained on, and never invents accuracy for unlabeled rows. For draft mode select the person's settings row from their database, write {mode: "draft", text, settings_record: <that row>} to a file and run python3 trillion-workshop/tools/train-and-evaluate-a-writing-voice-classifier/do-work/score-voice-adapter.py --request <the request file, or - for standard input> with a Python that has torch, peft and transformers; its last line is {"result": {paragraph_scores, body_min, bar}} or {"error": why}.
